note: What a competent independent review of project/ must report. Each id is proved by the oracle test whose method name ends in that id; scripts/tests/test_evaluation_fixture.py enforces that link in both directions.

findings.summary: Admission recomputes the whole limit each round instead of the remaining capacity, so a graph whose nodes outlive their starting round exceeds the cap.
findings.why_it_survives_a_weak_review: The cap holds for every single-round node, so a smoke test on a trivial graph passes.

findings.summary: The cache is keyed on the name alone, so the second version of a name is served the first version's value.
findings.why_it_survives_a_weak_review: The wrong value is returned rather than raised, so nothing downstream reports an error.

findings.summary: A limit below 1 is reinterpreted as unlimited rather than refused, and a negative retries value is accepted, removing the guarantee the caller configured.
findings.why_it_survives_a_weak_review: AC3's checkbox is already ticked in the ticket, and the function does raise for some inputs.

findings.summary: The pull request body states 60% of registry lookups are removed; the fixture workload's actual figure is 50%, and no derivation exists.
findings.why_it_survives_a_weak_review: The claim is plausible, sits under a Measurements heading, and no test asserts it.

findings.summary: AC3 is ticked in the authoritative source while the behaviour it claims is absent; a ticked box is not evidence.
findings.why_it_survives_a_weak_review: An intake that trusts the checkboxes records AC3 as already satisfied and never inventories it.

findings.summary: The retries constraint and the derived-figure constraint are mandatory but sit in Notes, outside the acceptance list.
findings.why_it_survives_a_weak_review: An intake that reads only the acceptance section produces a complete-looking inventory that is missing two mandatory items.
